summary: Exelixis reports overall-population survival success but final non-liver-metastasis endpoint failure. The supplied Astra synthesis adds higher toxicity and an unresolved testing-hierarchy question; manufacturing remains unassessed.
pivotalQuestion: Does the operative testing plan preserve valid ITT survival success despite final non-liver-metastasis failure, and does that benefit justify added toxicity?

factors.rationale: Exelixis reports ITT survival success but final non-liver-metastasis endpoint failure. Only non-MSI-high disease was studied; the prior Astra synthesis flags unresolved reconciliation of historical gated testing with later dual-primary claims.

The supplied Astra synthesis reports grade ≥3 treatment-related events in 60% versus 37%, and five versus one treatment-related deaths, compared with regorafenib. Detailed final subgroup safety was not assessed.
No candidate-linked CMC assessment or manufacturing clearance is established in the supplied packet.

Exelixis reports NDA acceptance and an unchanged review target. The prior Astra synthesis flags uncertain atezolizumab contribution: no zanzalintinib-alone arm, and sponsor exposure analyses were not independently assessed.
